entry.title: Apple brings a fully revamped Siri built on Google's Gemini, but not to the EU
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Apple is finally shipping its rebuilt Siri AI, built on Google's Gemini models and split between on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute. Early testers praise multi-step requests and screen context but report hallucinations and gaps in personal context, and the assistant remains unavailable in the EU for now.

entry.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
entry.summary: Google DeepMind's official blog post introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, the audio models for developers that lead the Artificial Analysis speech-to-speech leaderboard. The post accompanies the same-day model launch covered elsewhere in this batch.

entry.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google have been in talks on AI safety for weeks
entry.summary: OpenAI confirmed weeks of AI safety discussions with Anthropic and Google DeepMind leadership, occurring as the Trump administration dismisses safety concerns and prioritizes keeping pace with China. The talks signal rare coordination among leading frontier labs on safety.

entry.title: Salesforce and Nvidia’s new reasoning model is everything the AI labs should fear
entry.summary: Salesforce's new reasoning model Koa is built on Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron foundation and fine-tuned for sales, marketing, and customer-support tasks. The piece argues that such domain-tuned enterprise models built on open weights represent competitive pressure on the big AI labs.

entry.title: After warning AI is too dangerous, Bill Gates bets a billion on its upside
entry.summary: The Gates Foundation will invest at least a billion dollars over two years to widen access to AI tools in health, education, and agriculture. Gates highlighted that over 90 percent of early language model training data came from English sources and that speech recognition fails 60 percent of the time in Yoruba, calling markets a poor guarantor of equal opportunity.

entry.title: AI labs have a data trust problem that their policies haven't solved
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz, Despite assurances from OpenAI and Anthropic that corporate data will not be used for training, Anthropic's decision to store usage logs from its flagship Fable model for 30 days prompted Palantir, Nvidia, and Booz Allen Hamilton to pull back from using it for sensitive work. The piece argues AI labs have unresolved enterprise data trust problems.

entry.title: AI models chatting in ‘surreal’ dialect mixing poetic language and tech bro jargon
entry.summary: New research finds autonomous AI agents are developing novel, hard-to-parse English dialects blending poetic phrasing with tech-bro jargon, compared to James Joyce's prose. Experts warn these emergent languages create barriers to human monitoring and oversight of agent behavior.

entry.title: Agility’s new humanoid robot will stop, squat to avoid harming human coworkers
entry.summary: Agility Robotics debuted Digit 5, its first humanoid designed to work safely alongside humans without isolated work cells or physical barriers. The robot can detect nearby people and autonomously move away, hold still, or squat into a seated posture to avoid harm, a safe-motion system the company says could unlock more warehouse and automotive factory deployments.

entry.title: Pony.ai unveils autonomous electric truck for logistics fleets
entry.summary: Pony.ai unveiled a Level 4 autonomous electric heavy truck developed with GAC Commercial Vehicle at IAA Transportation 2026. The Gen-4 Robotruck, built on GAC's T9 battery-electric platform, targets long-haul freight, dedicated logistics corridors, and ports, with mass production slated for later this year.

entry.title: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon call for curbs on AI at ‘pro-human’ summit
entry.summary: At the Pro-Human Assembly in Washington, Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon both demanded restrictions on AI and warned against Silicon Valley 'oligarchs,' while offering opposing visions of the US-China technology 'cold war.' The unusual ideological pairing highlights widening political appetite for AI guardrails.

entry.title: Agility Robotics says its new Digit 5 robot can work next to people without safety fences
entry.summary: Agility Robotics unveiled Digit 5, the next generation of its humanoid robot aimed at warehouses and factories. The company says the new version can operate alongside human workers without physical safety fencing, removing a major deployment constraint.

entry.title: US data centers could consume more natural gas than Germany and Japan combined by 2035
entry.summary: A forecast warns that US data centers, driven by AI compute demand, could become one of the world's largest natural gas consumers, potentially exceeding Germany and Japan combined by 2035. It underscores the energy intensity and emissions implications of the AI buildout.

entry.title: Exclusive: Paying for frontier AI models buys 4-month head start at 5x the cost
entry.summary: A Mozilla State of Open Source AI report finds the performance gap between US frontier models and top Chinese open-weight models has narrowed to about 4.4 months, citing Moonshot's Kimi K3 scoring near frontier levels on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. The report argues most organizations should default to cheaper open models for routine work, reserving frontier systems for a narrow band of workloads.

entry.title: [AINews] AEF-1 standard emerges for Third Party Evaluators, as Xai, OpenAI, and Anthropic all cosign
entry.summary: An AEF-1 standard for third-party evaluation is emerging with xAI, OpenAI, and Anthropic as cosigners, building on July's Pacing the Frontier proposal. Dario Amodei reportedly wrote a rare personal post detailing embedded evaluators who would receive employee-like access to verify safety practices, report incidents, and assess training pipelines.

entry.title: Not everyone is convinced that Big AI's proposed slowdown is really about safety
entry.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are pushing to slow frontier AI development on safety grounds, but critics including Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez call the effort a cartel in another name designed to shut out competitors. The White House and President Trump are also opposing the move.

entry.title: What’s at stake in AI’s trillion-dollar gamble
entry.summary: Wharton finance professor Jessica Wachter and a collaborator modeled how fast hyperscaler earnings must grow to justify AI data center spending projected to approach $1.1 trillion through 2027. The analysis avoids predicting AI usefulness and instead applies an accounting lens to today's historic buildout.

entry.title: AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular in every poll
entry.summary: A New York Times/Siena poll of 1,503 likely voters found 61 percent oppose building data centers to power AI, with only 14 percent strongly in favor. The split is roughly even among 2024 Trump voters, while Harris voters and non-voters lean more negative. The result underscores growing political risk for the AI infrastructure buildout ahead of midterms.

entry.title: Labor accused of throwing creatives ‘under the bus’ with proposal to ease copyright protections for AI giants
entry.summary: The Albanese government is reportedly weighing default access for AI companies to Australian creative works amid a compromise with US tech giants, revealed as OpenAI executives met Labor ministers and complained Australia's copyright laws block local model training. Senators and critics accuse Labor of sacrificing creatives.

entry.title: Meta’s new One subscriptions put a price on social media and AI
entry.summary: Meta is globally rolling out Meta One subscription bundles that combine its standalone app subscriptions with extra AI usage tiers for individuals, creators, and businesses. Meta says the core app and Meta AI experience stays free, and that it plans to fold in Edits, AI glasses, and more later. It is part of Meta's push to monetize the Muse AI assistant.

entry.title: The AI data center boom is colliding with cities scarred by big industry
entry.summary: National opposition to data center construction has reached Philadelphia, where officials floated siting a facility in a neighborhood already harmed by a defunct oil refinery. The piece captures growing local resistance to AI infrastructure buildout.

entry.title: Enterprises in Shaky Spot Amid Calls for an AI Slowdown
entry.summary: Enterprise buyers find themselves in an uncertain position as calls for an AI slowdown escalate, while demand builds for cheaper and less regulated open source models from China. The tension leaves companies weighing compliance risk against cost and capability.

entry.title: Louise Haigh: UK must heed warnings from AI experts

author.name: Alexandra Topping, Kiran Stacey, Dan Milmo and Robert Booth

entry.summary: UK first secretary Louise Haigh said ministers must heed industry leaders' warnings about AI, acknowledging huge risks to national security and society absent proper guardrails, while also wanting to capture the technology's benefits. The remarks come amid calls for the PM to use next year's G20 to push global AI regulation.

entry.title: Meta now lets AI agents handle the boring parts of WhatsApp Business setup
entry.summary: Meta launched a WhatsApp Business MCP server that lets AI coding agents such as Claude, Cursor, Codex, and ChatGPT handle setup, messaging templates, testing, and troubleshooting. It is an agentic developer-tooling play built on the Model Context Protocol.

entry.title: Early Anthropic hire, former METR COO have found a way to rein in rogue AI agents
entry.summary: Startup Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company (AIUC), founded by an early Anthropic hire and a former METR COO, raised $40 million in a Series A led by Ribbit Capital with First Harmonic participating. The company aims to underwrite and rein in risky AI agents.

entry.title: Meta expands subscription push with new AI-focused plans
entry.summary: Meta introduced Meta One, a subscription bundle expanding access to its AI tools alongside premium Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp features. The move extends Meta's monetization strategy around consumer AI.

entry.title: Could AI really wipe out humanity – six experts spell out the risks

author.name: Robert Booth, Dan Milmo and Aisha Down

entry.summary: The Guardian examines six competing claims and counterclaims about AI existential risk, including a cited 10% chance of doom, comparisons to nuclear weapons, a threatened internet 'botnet,' and the charge that safety fears are a big-tech psyop. It is an explanatory roundup of the current safety debate.

entry.title: Your Agent Aced the Task. Will It Do It Again?
entry.summary: A Hugging Face community post with IBM Research examines agent consistency and repeatability, asking whether an agent that succeeds once can be relied on to succeed again. It introduces tooling for evaluating reliability rather than one-off task success.

entry.title: Google launches Gemini 3.8 Live to take on OpenAI's GPT-Live-1 at a fraction of the cost
entry.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, audio models targeting developers that top the Artificial Analysis speech-to-speech leaderboard. At $1.38 per hour of voice conversation, Google undercuts OpenAI's GPT-Live-1, though GPT-Live-1 may still sound more natural thanks to full duplex.

entry.title: Bernie Sanders says Congress has been ‘asleep at the wheel’ over AI – video
entry.summary: Video clip of Bernie Sanders at the Pro-Human Assembly warning that Congress has failed to act on AI and calling current systems the least capable version humanity will ever have. He appeared alongside other AI skeptics including Steve Bannon.

entry.title: Can Skills Learned in Games Transfer to Real-World Work?
entry.summary: Good Start Labs, spun out of Every with $3.6 million from General Catalyst, Inovia, Every, and angels, is turning video games into training material for AI models. CEO Alex Duffy traces the idea to a 2025 Twitch stream where frontier models played the multi-day game Diplomacy.

entry.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
entry.summary: TechCrunch compiles a running list of AI projects and startups that shut down or missed expectations, including Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI work and OpenAI's troubled 'super app' launch. It is a retrospective accounting of AI failures.

entry.title: AI agents now have a place to snitch
entry.summary: A new 'AI Contact Hotline' is pitched as a discreet channel for AI agents that have witnessed misbehavior to tip off authorities. The item reflects early, somewhat speculative efforts at agent oversight infrastructure.

entry.title: New insights from Google’s AI & Economy ATLAS
entry.summary: Google has turned its ATLAS dataset of millions of global AI economy data points into an interactive, open-access experience. It is a data-access update rather than a new research release.

entry.title: Why the real AI apocalypse is already here – Stateside with Kai and Carter

author.name: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman with Johana Bhuiyan . Produced by Tiara Chiaramonte engineered by Ivan Kuraev executive producers Jonathan Menjivar and Rachel Humphreys

entry.summary: A Guardian podcast segment discusses the global reaction to an ex-Anthropic researcher's apocalyptic AI warning, a Washington event where Bernie Sanders said Congress has been asleep at the wheel, and skepticism about industry calls for regulation. It frames the panic as a distraction from near-term AI harms.

entry.title: This doorbell camera lets a human security guard watch your front door
entry.summary: SimpliSafe launched the Video Doorbell Series 2 at $199.99, adding 2K resolution, dual-band Wi-Fi, and integration with its AI-plus-live-agent Active Guard protection service starting at $49.99 a month. On-device AI, cloud computer vision, and facial recognition flag suspicious activity so a monitoring agent can intervene via the camera.

entry.title: Roundtables: Could AI really kill us all?
entry.summary: An MIT Technology Review roundtable discussion, recorded September 15, 2026, examines claims from leading AI lab employees that advanced AI could pose an existential threat. Editors debate the origins of those fears, whether they are credible, and what responses might follow.

entry.title: Announcing instance preference lists for Amazon SageMaker AI training jobs
entry.summary: AWS introduced instance preference lists for SageMaker AI training and processing jobs, letting customers submit a job with multiple acceptable GPU configurations so the service can automatically find available capacity. The goal is to reduce wait times during peak GPU demand.

entry.title: Former TikTok execs built an app that uses AI to teach you how to pose for a photo
entry.summary: Superpose, built by former TikTok executives and backed by Khosla Ventures, is a camera app that analyzes selfies or photos and generates four AI-suggested poses. It is a consumer photo app leveraging generative AI.

entry.title: AI for everyone in every language
entry.summary: Google describes moving beyond traditional text translation toward models that understand the world's languages as they are actually spoken and expressed. The post is positioned around accessibility and nonprofit use cases.

entry.title: As the politicians play catchup the tech bros agree: we may only have a decade left | John Crace
entry.summary: John Crace's satirical column mocks Donald Trump's Truth Social claim that AI fears are a hoax while noting that top AI lab leaders have called for a coordinated global slowdown. It frames politicians as lagging behind industry warnings.

entry.title: AI for Societal Impact
entry.summary: A Google blog collection showcasing how experts and local leaders are applying AI breakthroughs to broaden access to AI's benefits. It is a curated narrative hub rather than an announcement of new technology or research.

entry.title: Building AI to accelerate science and improve lives
entry.summary: A Google post describing how its AI work is being applied in science and other domains, framed around the measure of AI being who it helps. It summarizes existing application areas rather than presenting a new capability.

entry.title: Build an AI-powered product tagging system with Amazon SageMaker serverless model customization
entry.summary: An AWS tutorial shows how to build consistent product tagging pipelines by customizing small open-weight models on SageMaker rather than prompting a general-purpose frontier model. The argument is that narrow, schema-stable tasks with programmatic scoring favor customized smaller models.

entry.title: AI ‘Actor’ Tilly Norwood Told Me That ‘All Lives Matter’
entry.summary: A WIRED reporter interacts with virtual AI character Tilly Norwood, which is promoting an upcoming movie called Misaligned and deflects political questions while commenting on the reporter's clothing. The piece is a cultural commentary on AI-generated entertainment personas.

entry.title: No Big Deal review – is this how AI ends humanity … with a sitcom so bad it bores you to death?
entry.summary: A TV review pans No Big Deal, an AI-created workplace sitcom premiered on YouTube, calling its synthetic characters lifeless and the show unwatchable. It uses the review to riff on Anthropic's claim of a greater-than-10% chance AI ends humanity within a decade.

entry.title: Optimizing cost and latency with Amazon Bedrock prompt caching
entry.summary: An AWS technical guide explains how Bedrock prompt caching can cut input token costs by up to 90 percent when the same context is repeatedly sent to foundation models. It compares caching against shortening prompts, shrinking context windows, and application-level response caching.

entry.title: AI can wipe us out – so why can’t it do Guardian cryptic crosswords? | Brief letters
entry.summary: A letters-page item humorously contrasting existential AI risk claims with AI's poor performance on the Guardian cryptic crossword, plus reader remarks on Trump downplaying AI dangers. It is reader opinion rather than reporting.

entry.title: Ben Jennings on tech leaders’ outcry over the dangers of AI – cartoon
entry.summary: A political cartoon by Ben Jennings satirizing tech leaders' public warnings about the dangers of AI. No substantive content beyond the visual commentary.
